_source.draft: olumi-work/recovery/s3/T6-prompt/raw/B/D4-reduce-cycle-time-r2-call1.json (provider output, gpt-5.6-terra, CEE a770ce49 + AIE manifest b34d6ebb), output_text parsed verbatim

brief: Our current median delivery cycle is 8 weeks. Without a change, we expect it to reach 10 weeks next quarter. We want to reduce it by at least 15% relative to today's 8-week level by the end of that quarter. We are considering test automation or a release coordinator. Automation may initially slow delivery; the coordinator could help but hiring time is uncertain. We must not worsen the current defect rate. Help us understand the causal trade-offs.

basis.effect_unit: weeks at the end of next quarter
also_required: must not worsen the current defect rate

factors.label: No-change cycle increase by next quarter

links.basis: More automated regression checking is estimated to remove 0.4 weeks of cycle time per additional 10 percentage points of coverage by quarter end.
Automated repeatable testing is estimated to prevent 0.5 percentage points of defects per additional 10 percentage points of coverage.
A full-time coordinator is provisionally estimated to remove one week of scheduling and release hand-off delay by quarter end.
Dedicated release readiness coordination is estimated to reduce escaped defects by 0.5 percentage points.
Each additional percentage point of defects is provisionally estimated to add 0.2 weeks of rework and verification time.

links.from: No-change cycle increase by next quarter
links.basis: Derived from the stated no-change forecast: the cycle rises from 8 weeks today to 10 weeks next quarter, or 2 additional weeks.

unknowns: Forecast source retained: "Without a change, we expect it to reach 10 weeks next quarter." This is modelled as a shared external increase of 2 weeks from today's 8-week level by the end of next quarter.
The exact calendar end date of "next quarter" is needed to confirm the three-month planning horizon.
What is the current defect rate, and how is it measured? The provisional 5% baseline is an Olumi modelling assumption, not a reported measurement.
How much automation coverage is feasible by the end of next quarter, and how much delivery capacity will its initial implementation consume?
How long would recruiting, notice, onboarding, and ramp-up take for the release coordinator? The coordinator benefit is currently a provisional quarter-end estimate.
The link sizes are provisional modelling assumptions; they should be replaced with your delivery, defect, and hiring evidence before relying on a calculation.
draft.decision_question: Help us understand the causal trade-offs.

aie_operations.old: Set `decision_question` to the question the brief asks, copied VERBATIM from the brief (only the question itself, without any lead-in clause), or null if it asks none. Never reword it.
aie_operations.replacement: Set decision_question to the brief's governing question or statement of intent, copied VERBATIM as one span of 8–240 characters, including a statement such as 'We need to decide whether ...'. Preserve its compound purposes and conditions. Use null only when no such span exists. Never reword it or turn exploration into a decision.

aie_operations.location: actual provider body.text.format.schema.properties.decision_question.description where retained by strict schema
aie_operations.old: The question the brief asks, copied VERBATIM from the brief (only the question itself, without any lead-in clause), or null if it asks none.
aie_operations.replacement: The brief's own governing question or statement of intent, copied VERBATIM as one span of 8–240 characters. Include statements such as 'We need to decide whether ...'. Keep every purpose and condition within that span. Use null only when the brief contains no such span. Do not reword it or turn exploration into a decision.

aie_operations.anchor: Preserve exact user facts, numbers, constraint semantics and time horizon.
aie_operations.insertion: NO-CHANGE FORECAST. When the brief gives both a current level and a forecast without an intervention at a later horizon, preserve both with their distinct references and the forecast's exact wording and qualifiers. Represent the forecast once as a shared external drift by that horizon, in the goal's own units, using the existing factor and definitional-link shape. Derive the drift as forecast minus current level and identify it as derived from the stated forecast, never as a newly stated measurement. For 8 weeks today and a forecast of 10 weeks next quarter, retain 8 weeks as today's level and a forecast of 2 additional weeks by that horizon. That forecast affects carrying on and the alternatives unless an alternative changes its cause. Do not replace today's level or the target with the forecast, set the forecast drift to zero, count it twice, or retain it only as a question. Keep the original forecast sentence and its source alongside the derived change in the available evidence and question carriers.

aie_d4_fields.baseline_known_description: True only for a baseline supplied by the user or supported evidence. A provisional AI estimate keeps this false. EXCEPTION: a factor defined as a CHANGE FROM TODAY may be 0 today by definition; that does not state its value at a future horizon. For the existing NO-CHANGE FORECAST representation, derive the future change as the stated no-change forecast at its specified horizon minus the supported current level of the SAME quantity, with compatible units and reference. Preserve both sources, the horizon and conditions. Do not apply today's structural-zero exception to this future value: a valid derived change may be positive, negative or zero. Identify it as a derived conditional forecast, not a newly stated measurement or observed current level. Missing or incompatible operands remain unknown; never invent a value or probability law.
aie_d4_fields.definitional_description: true ONLY when this link holds BY DEFINITION, not by estimate: the source is a defined contribution to the target's own quantity, in the SAME unit and reference, so one unit of the source contributes exactly one unit to the target (money lost to a risk is money the goal does not get: effect_amount -1, effect_per_source_change 1; a supported derived no-change forecast change contributes one for one to that SAME quantity at its stated horizon: effect_amount 1, effect_per_source_change 1). The forecast case is an additive modelling definition, not a causal size estimated from two levels. Preserve the signed change, the original current level and forecast conditions, and count the shared change once. Do not set this for another quantity, an ordinary causal hypothesis or a unit/reference mismatch. null for every other link.

exact_whole_descriptions.baseline_known: True only for a baseline supplied by the user or supported evidence. A provisional AI estimate keeps this false. EXCEPTION: for a factor explicitly defined as a CHANGE FROM TODAY, today's structural value is 0: baseline_known true, baseline_value 0. This is a definition, not a newly stated measurement, and does not state its value at a future horizon. For the existing NO-CHANGE FORECAST representation, derive the future change as the stated no-change forecast at its specified horizon minus the supported current level of the SAME quantity, with compatible units and reference. Preserve both sources, the horizon and conditions. Do not apply today's structural-zero exception to this future value: a valid derived change may be positive, negative or zero. Identify it as a derived conditional forecast, not a newly stated measurement or observed current level. Missing or incompatible operands remain unknown; never invent a value or probability law.
exact_whole_descriptions.goal_source_quote: For a target actually stated in the brief, including a stated event or deliverable, copy the complete relevant statement VERBATIM. Preserve any stated speaker, subject, figure, comparator, unit, reference, denominator, period, qualifications, conditions and negation. Include consecutive complete sentences when they are needed for that meaning; do not shorten qualifications, stitch unrelated passages or add words or a speaker name not present in the source. null when the brief states no target. A quote does not itself verify the claim, create a numerical target or confirm that its complete meaning is saved.
exact_whole_descriptions.link_source_quote: For a relation claimed as stated in the brief (provenance explicit), copy its complete applicable statement VERBATIM, preserving any stated speaker, both directed subjects, its size if supplied, and all units, reference, period, qualifications, conditions and negation. Include consecutive complete sentences when needed; never invent an endpoint, direction, size or speaker, shorten qualifications or stitch unrelated passages. null when no applicable stated relation exists. Preserve attributed or disputed views as such; do not turn a question, denial or superseded statement into a current unqualified causal claim. Quote presence or a shared figure alone does not verify the relation's meaning or authorship.
exact_whole_descriptions.unknown_concerns: One entry for each entry in unknowns, in the same order: copy the complete question exactly and identify what every substantive part is about. concerns lists only the EXACT declared labels of the goal, factors, options, risks or outcomes, with a directed link written as "<from label> → <to label>". Include referents in quoted facts, ranges, forecasts, qualifications, conditions or dissent within the question. Use an empty list when the question concerns the model as a whole or its complete meaning cannot be bound uniquely to the declared labels and directed pairs. Never invent a label, guess a link from a shared number or omit a substantive referent. These are proposed bindings, not evidence that a question is resolved or may be removed.

one_reached_instruction_delta.old_clause: set the forecast drift to zero
one_reached_instruction_delta.replacement_clause: replace a supported non-zero future change with today's structural zero
